		<p style="margin:11pt 0pt 5pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">The fair value of these restricted stock units was determined based on a combination, where applicable, of the closing price of the Company&#x2019;s common stock on the trading date immediately prior to the grant date for units subject to performance conditions, or at its Monte-Carlo simulation value for units subject to market conditions.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company recognizes compensation expense for the portion of the targeted performance-based restricted stock units subject to market conditions even if the condition is never satisfied.&nbsp;However, if the performance conditions are not met for the portion of the targeted performance-based restricted stock units subject to such performance conditions, no compensation expense will be recognized, and any previously recognized compensation expense will be reversed.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:11pt 0pt 5pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Accounting for Income Taxes </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Deferred tax assets generally represent items that will result in a tax deduction in future years for which we have already recorded the tax benefit in our income statement. We assess the likelihood that deferred tax assets will be recovered from future taxable income. To the extent we believe that recovery is not probable, a valuation allowance is established. To the extent we establish a valuation allowance or increase this allowance, we must include an expense as part of the income tax provision in our results of operations</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Our deferred tax asset balances in our consolidated balance sheets were $</font><font style="display: inline;">285.2 million and $364.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million as of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively. Our valuation allowances for deferred tax assets in our consolidated balance sheets were $</font><font style="display: inline;">95.3 million and $77.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million as of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In addition, significant judgment is required in determining and assessing the impact of certain tax-related contingencies. We establish accruals when, despite our belief that our tax return positions are fully supportable, it is probable that we have incurred a loss related to tax contingencies and the loss or range of loss can be reasonably estimated. We adjust the accruals related to tax contingencies as part of our provision for income taxes in our results of operations based upon changing facts and circumstances, such as progress of a tax audit, development of industry related examination issues, as well as legislative, regulatory or judicial developments. A number of years may elapse before a particular matter, for which we have established an accrual, is audited and resolved.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The first step in determining the deferred tax asset valuation allowance is identifying reporting jurisdictions where we have a history of tax and operating losses or are projected to have losses in future periods as a result of changes in operational performance. We then determine if a valuation allowance should be established against the deferred tax assets for that reporting jurisdiction.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The second step is to determine the amount of the valuation allowance. We will generally establish a valuation allowance equal to the net deferred tax asset (deferred tax assets less deferred tax liabilities) related to the jurisdiction identified in step one of the analysis. In certain cases, we may not reduce the valuation allowance by the amount of the deferred tax liabilities depending on the nature and timing of future taxable income attributable to deferred tax liabilities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In assessing tax contingencies, we apply the provisions of ASC 740-10, &#x201C;Income Taxes&#x201D;. We apply the recognition threshold and measurement of a tax position taken or expected to be taken in a tax return and follow the guidance on various matters such as derecognition, interest, penalties and disclosure. We classify interest and penalties as a component of income tax expense.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During each reporting period, we assess the facts and circumstances related to recorded tax contingencies. If tax contingencies are no longer deemed probable based upon new facts and circumstances, the contingency is reflected as a reduction of the provision for income taxes in the current period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our deferred tax </font><font style="display: inline;">assets</font><font style="display: inline;"> exceeded our deferred tax </font><font style="display: inline;">labilities</font><font style="display: inline;"> by $</font><font style="display: inline;">63.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million as of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">, excluding the impact of valuation allowances. Historically, we have produced federal taxable income, and as such, we believe that the likelihood of not realizing the federal tax benefit of our deferred tax assets is remote. However, we do have subsidiaries with a history of tax losses in certain state jurisdictions and, based upon those historical tax losses, we assumed that the subsidiaries would not be profitable in the future for those states&#x2019; tax purposes. If our assertion regarding the future profitability of those subsidiaries was incorrect, then our deferred tax assets would be understated by the amount of the state valuation allowance of </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">95.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;"> at December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The </font><font style="display: inline;">IRS</font><font style="display: inline;"> may propose adjustments for items we have failed to identify as tax contingencies. If the IRS were to propose and</font><font style="display: inline;"> sustain assessments equal to 10</font><font style="display: inline;">% of our taxable income for 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">, we would incur approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">9.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;"> of additional tax payments for 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;"> plus interest and penalties, if applicable.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">Additionally, on December 22, 2017, the Tax Act was signed into law. The Tax Act significantly revises the U.S. corporate income tax by, among other things, lowering the statutory corporate tax rate from 35% to 21% and eliminating certain deductions</font><font style="display: inline;">. Due to the timing of the enactment and the complexity involved in applying the provisions of the Tax Act</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">we have </font><font style="display: inline;">made reasonable estimates of the effects of the Tax Act on our existing deferred tax assets and liabilities and recognized a provisional benefit for income taxes of $18.0 million, or $0.44 earnings per diluted share, for the year ended December 31, 2017. As we complete our analysis of the Tax Act, including the collection of data and interpretation of any additional guidance issued by the U.S. Treasury Department, the IRS, and other standard-setting bodies, we may make adjustments to the provisional amounts. Those adjustments may materially impact our provision for income taxes in the period in which the adjustments are made.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Segment Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 10pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We </font><font style="display: inline;">provide healthcare services primarily through our ownership and operation of community hospitals and regional health systems, certain of which provide related healthcare services through </font><font style="display: inline;">physician practices, outpatient centers, and post-acute facilities</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> Accordingly, w</font><font style="display: inline;">e &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">have</font><font style="display: inline;"> one operating segment, healthcare services, for segment reporting purposes in accordance with ASC 280-10, &#x201C;S</font><font style="display: inline;">egment Reporting&#x201D;. Additionally, we have one reporting unit for goodwill impairment testing in accordance with </font><font style="display: inline;">ASC 350-10.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Inflation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The healthcare industry is labor-intensive. Wages and other expenses increase during periods of inflation and when labor shortages in marketplaces occur. In addition, suppliers pass along rising costs to us in the form of higher prices. Private insurers pass along their rising costs in the form of lower reimbursement to us. Our ability to pass on these increased costs in increased rates is limited because of increasing regulatory and competitive pressures and the fact that the majority of our revenues are fee-based. Accordingly, inflationary pressures could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Ite</font><a name="MarketRisk"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">m 7A. </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Interest Rates</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 5pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The following discussion relates to our exposure to market risk based on changes in interest rates:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 5pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Outstanding Debt</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">, we had outstanding debt, excluding unamortized </font><font style="display: inline;">debt issuance costs and premium, </font><font style="display: inline;">of $</font><font style="display: inline;">2,918.3 </font><font style="display: inline;">million, </font><font style="display: inline;">23.1</font><font style="display: inline;">%, or $</font><font style="display: inline;">673.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, of which was subject to variable rates of interest.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">If the </font><font style="display: inline;">interest rate</font><font style="display: inline;"> on our </font><font style="display: inline;">variable rate </font><font style="display: inline;">long-term debt </font><font style="display: inline;">outstanding as of December 31, 2017 was 100 basis points higher </font><font style="display: inline;">during the year ended December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">, our net income would </font><font style="display: inline;">have </font><font style="display: inline;">decreas</font><font style="display: inline;">ed</font><font style="display: inline;"> by approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;">4.3 </font><font style="display: inline;">million, or $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.10</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">loss </font><font style="display: inline;">per diluted share.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 5pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Cash Balances</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Certain of our outstanding cash balances are invested overnight with high credit quality financial institutions. We do not hold direct investments in auction rate securities, collateralized debt obligations, structured investment vehicles or mortgage-backed securities. We do not have significant exposure to changing interest rates on invested cash at </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2017</font><font style="display: inline;">. As a result, the interest rate market risk implicit in these investments at </font><font style="display: inline;">December 31, 2017</font><font style="display: inline;">, if any, is low.</font>
		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Manag</font><a name="ManagementsReport"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">ement&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Management of LifePoint Health, Inc. is responsible for the preparation, integrity and fair presentation of its published consolidated financial statements. The financial statements have been prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles and, as such, include amounts based on judgments and estimates made by management. The Company also prepared the other information included in the annual report and is responsible for its accuracy and consistency with the consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Management is also responsible for establishing and maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting. The Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that pertain to the Company&#x2019;s ability to record, process, summarize and report reliable financial data. The Company maintains a system of internal control over financial reporting, which is designed to provide reasonable assurance to the Company&#x2019;s management and Board of Directors regarding the preparation of reliable published financial statements and safeguarding of the Company&#x2019;s assets. The system includes a documented organizational structure and division of responsibility, established policies and procedures, including a code of conduct to foster a strong ethical climate, which are communicated throughout the Company, and the careful selection, training and development of our people.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Board of Directors, acting through its Audit and Compliance Committee, is responsible for the oversight of the Company&#x2019;s accounting policies, financial reporting and internal control. The Audit and Compliance Committee of the Board of Directors is comprised entirely of outside directors who are independent of management. The Audit and Compliance Committee is responsible for the appointment and compensation of the independent registered public accounting firm. It meets periodically with management, the independent registered public accounting firm and the internal auditors to ensure that they are carrying out their responsibilities. The Audit and Compliance Committee is also responsible for performing an oversight role by reviewing and monitoring the financial, accounting and auditing procedures of the Company in addition to reviewing the Company&#x2019;s financial reports. Internal auditors monitor the operation of the internal control system and report findings and recommendations to management and the Audit and Compliance Committee. Corrective actions are taken to address control deficiencies and other opportunities for improving the internal control system as they are identified. The independent registered public accounting firm and the internal auditors have full and unlimited access to the Audit and Compliance Committee, with or without management, to discuss the adequacy of internal control over financial reporting, and any other matters which they believe should be brought to the attention of the Audit and Compliance Committee.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Management recognizes that there are inherent limitations in the effectiveness of any system of internal control over financial reporting, including the possibility of human error and the circumvention or overriding of internal control. Accordingly, even effective internal control over financial reporting can provide only reasonable assurance with respect to financial statement preparation and may not prevent or detect misstatements. Further, because of changes in conditions, the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting may vary over time.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company assessed its internal control system as of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;"> in relation to criteria for effective internal control over financial reporting described in &#x201C;Internal Control&nbsp;&#x2014;&nbsp;Integrated Framework&#x201D; issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework). Based on its assessment, the Company has determined that, as of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">, its system of internal control over financial reporting was effective.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The consolidated financial statements have been audited by the independent registered public accounting firm of Ernst &amp; Young LLP, which was given unrestricted access to all financial records and related data, including minutes of all meetings of stockholders, the Board of Directors and committees of the Board. Reports of the independent registered public accounting firm, which includes the independent registered public accounting firm&#x2019;s attestation report on the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting, are also presented within this document.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>

					<p style="margin:0pt 0.8pt 0pt 18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;height:1.00pt;overflow:hidden;font-size: 10pt">
						<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font></p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">Rep</font><a name="Report1"></a><font style="display: inline;">ort of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 20.9pt 8pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Board of Directors and Stockholders</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 20.9pt 8pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">LifePoint Health, Inc.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 20.9pt 8pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 20.9pt 8pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Opinion on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We have audited LifePoint Health, Inc.&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2017, based on criteria established in Internal Control&#x2014;Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework) (the COSO criteria). In our opinion, LifePoint Health, Inc. (the Company) maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2017, based on the COSO criteria.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (PCAOB), the consolidated balance sheets of LifePoint Health, Inc. as of December 31, 2017 and 2016, and the related consolidated statements of income, comprehensive income, stockholders&#x2019; </font><font style="display: inline;">equity</font><font style="display: inline;">, and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2017</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">and t</font><font style="display: inline;">he related notes and our report</font><font style="display: inline;"> and our report dated February 23, 2018 expressed an unqualified opinion thereon.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 20.9pt 8pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Basis for Opinion</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting included in the accompanying Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting based on our audit. We are a public accounting firm registered with the PCAOB and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 20.9pt 8pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Definition and Limitations of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">A company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company&#x2019;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 20.9pt 8pt 180pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">/s/ Ernst &amp; Young LLP</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 20.9pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&#xFEFF;</font>

		</p>

We are a public accounting firm registered with the PCAOB and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font>

Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Organization</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 5pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">LifePoint Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation, acting through its subsidiaries, owns and operates community hospitals, regional health systems, physician practices, outpatient centers, and post-acute facilities in </font><font style="display: inline;">22</font><font style="display: inline;"> states throughout the United States (&#x201C;U.S.&#x201D;). Unless the context otherwise indicates, LifePoint Health, Inc. and its subsidiaries are referred to herein as &#x201C;LifePoint&#x201D; or the &#x201C;Company.&#x201D; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Principles of Consolidation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The accompanying consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company and all subsidiaries and entities controlled by the Company through the Company&#x2019;s direct or indirect ownership of a majority interest and exclusive rights granted to the Company as the sole general partner or controlling member of such entities, including Duke LifePoint Healthcare, a joint venture between LifePoint and a wholly-controlled affiliate of Duke University Health System, Inc., and the Regional Health Network of Kentucky and Southern Indiana, a joint venture between LifePoint and Norton Healthcare, Inc.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the Company consolidates any entities for which it receives the majority of the entity&#x2019;s expected returns or is at risk for the majority of the entity&#x2019;s expected losses based upon its investment or financial interest in the entity.&nbsp;&nbsp;All significant intercompany accounts and transactions within the Company have been eliminated in consolidation.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In connection with certain acquisitions, the Company has entered into agreements to provide management and administrative support for the operations of </font><font style="display: inline;">seven</font><font style="display: inline;"> hospitals.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has concluded that these hospitals qualify as variable interest entities in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification (&#x201C;ASC&#x201D;) 810-10 &#x201C;Consolidations&#x201D; and, due to its economic interest in these hospitals combined with its agreements to provide management and administrative support, it is the primary beneficiary.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, the Company has consolidated the operations of these seven hospitals.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company accounts for its investments in entities in which the Company exhibits significant influence, but not control, in accordance with the equity method of accounting.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not consolidate its equity method investments, but rather measures them at their initial costs and then subsequently adjusts their carrying values through income for their respective shares of the earnings or losses during the period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Use of Estimates</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#x201C;GAAP&#x201D;) requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the Company&#x2019;s accompanying consolidated financial statements and notes to consolidated financial statements. Actual results could differ from those estimates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">General and Administrative Costs</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The majority of the Company&#x2019;s expenses are &#x201C;cost of revenue&#x201D; items. Costs that could be classified as &#x201C;general and administrative&#x201D; by the Company would include its health support center overhead costs, which were </font><font style="display: inline;">$232.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;m</font><font style="display: inline;">illion, $</font><font style="display: inline;">223.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and $</font><font style="display: inline;">235.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million for the years ended December 31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In accordance with ASC 825-10, &#x201C;Financial Instruments&#x201D;, the fair value of the Company&#x2019;s financial instruments are further described as follows.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Cash and Cash Equivalents, Accounts Receivable and Accounts Payable</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The carrying amounts reported in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets for cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable and accounts payable approximate fair value because of the short-term maturity of these instruments.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The fair values of the Company&#x2019;s long-term debt instruments were estimated based on the average bid and ask price as determined using published rates and categorized as Level 2 within the fair value hierarchy in accordance with ASC 820-10, &#x201C;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures&#x201D; (&#x201C;ASC 820-10&#x201D;).&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition and Accounts Receivable</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Overview</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company recognizes revenues in the period in which services are performed. Accounts receivable primarily consist of amounts due </font><font style="display: inline;">from third-party paye</font><font style="display: inline;">rs and patients. The Company&#x2019;s ability to collect outstanding receivables is critical to its results of operations and cash flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;Amounts the Company receives for treatment of patients covered by governmental programs such as Medicare and Med</font><font style="display: inline;">icaid and other third-party paye</font><font style="display: inline;">rs such as health maintenance organizations (&#x201C;HMOs&#x201D;), preferred provider organizations (&#x201C;PPOs&#x201D;) and other private insurers are generally less than the Company&#x2019;s established billing rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, to provide for accounts receivable that could become uncollectible in the future, the Company establishes an allowance for doubtful accounts to reduce the carrying value of such receivables to their estimated net realizable value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, the revenues and accounts receivable reported in the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements are recorded at the net amount expected to be received.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Change in Accounting Estimate</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During the year ended December 31, 2017, the Company recorded an increase to its provision for doubtful accounts of </font><font style="display: inline;">$72.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$46.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million net of income taxes, or </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.13</font><font style="display: inline;"> loss per diluted share, </font><font style="display: inline;">as a result of a change in its accounting estimate of the collectability of accounts receivable.&nbsp; The Company is in the process of installing new systems, developing enhanced analytical procedures and updating its </font><font style="display: inline;">estimation processes</font><font style="display: inline;"> in order to centralize and standardize its processes for estimating the collectability of these accounts.&nbsp; In connection with these implementation efforts, the Company identified additional information which indicated that its current collection estimates might be different from its historical collection estimates.&nbsp; Management utilized this new information to further refine its estimation procedures to more precisely estimate the collectability of accounts receivable at a more detailed and disaggregated level.&nbsp; The Company&#x2019;s change in its estimation procedures of the collectability of its accounts receivable is considered a change in accounting estimate in accordance with ASC 250-10 &#x201C;Accounting Changes and Error Corrections.&#x201D;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">When adjusted to exclude the impact of the </font><font style="display: inline;">$72.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million </font><font style="display: inline;">increase </font><font style="display: inline;">to the provision for doubtful accounts </font><font style="display: inline;">during the year ended December 31, 2017 </font><font style="display: inline;">as a result of a change in accounting estimate,</font><font style="display: inline;"> the Company&#x2019;s revenues before provision for doubtful accounts from Medicare, Medicaid and HMOs, PPOs and other private insurers for the year ended December 31, 2017 represented </font><font style="display: inline;">38.2%</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">15.0%</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">46.4%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of revenues, respectively, and its provision for doubtful accounts for the year ended December 31, 2017 represented </font><font style="display: inline;">14.1%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of revenues.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Contractual Discounts and Cost Report Settlements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company derives a significant portion of its revenues from M</font><font style="display: inline;">edicare, Medicaid and other paye</font><font style="display: inline;">rs that receive discounts from its established billing rates. The Company must estimate the total amount of these discounts to prepare its consolidated financial statements. The Medicare and Medicaid regulations and various managed care contracts under which these discounts must be calculated are complex and are subject to interpretation and adjustment. The Company estimates the allowance for</font><font style="display: inline;"> contractual discounts on a paye</font><font style="display: inline;">r-specific basis given its interpretation of the applicable regulations or contract terms. These interpretations sometimes result in payments that differ from the Company&#x2019;s estimates. Additionally, updated regulations and contract renegotiations occur frequently, necessitating regular review and assessment of the estimation process by management. Changes in estimates related to the allowance for contractual discounts affect revenues reported in the Company&#x2019;s accompanying consolidated statements of </font><font style="display: inline;">income</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Charity Care</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Self-pay revenues are derived primarily from patients who do not have any form of healthcare coverage.&nbsp;&nbsp;The revenues associated with self-pay patients are generally reported at the Company&#x2019;s gross charges. The Company evaluates these patients, after the patient&#x2019;s medical condition is determined to be stable, for their ability to pay based upon federal and state poverty guidelines, qualifications for Medicaid or other governmental assistance programs, as well as the local hospital&#x2019;s policy for charity care. The Company provides care without charge to certain patients that qualify under the local charity care policy of each of its hospitals. For the years ended December 31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, the Company estimates that its costs of care provided under its charity care programs approximated </font><font style="display: inline;">$27.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;m</font><font style="display: inline;">illion, </font><font style="display: inline;">$32.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$23.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not report a charity care patient&#x2019;s charges in revenues or in the provision for doubtful accounts as it is the Company&#x2019;s policy not to pursue collection of amo</font><font style="display: inline;">unts related to these patients.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s management estimates its costs of care provided under its charity care programs utilizing a calculated ratio of costs to gross charges multiplied by the Company&#x2019;s gross charity care charges provided.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s gross charity care charges include only services provided to patients who are unable to pay and qualify under the Company&#x2019;s local charity care policies.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent the Company receives reimbursement through the various governmental assistance programs in which it participates to subsidize its care of indigent patients, the Company does not include these patients&#x2019; charges in its cost of care provided under its charity care program.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Provision and Allowance for Doubtful Accounts</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">To provide for accounts receivable that could become uncollectible in the future, the Company establishes an allowance for doubtful accounts to reduce the carrying value of such receivables to their estimated net realizable value. The primary uncertainty lies with uninsured patient receivables and deductibles, co-payments or other amounts due from individual patients.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has an established process to determine the adequacy of the allowance for doubtful accounts that relies on a number of analytical tools and benchmarks to arrive at a reasonable allowance. No single statistic or measurement determines the adequacy of the allowance for doubtful accounts. Some of the analytical tools that the Company utilizes include, but are not limited to, historical cash collection ex</font><font style="display: inline;">perience, revenue trends by paye</font><font style="display: inline;">r classification and revenue days in accounts receivable.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accounts receivable are written off after collection efforts have been followed in accordance with the Company&#x2019;s policies.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">A summary of activity in the Company&#x2019;s allowance for doubtful accounts is as follows (in millions):</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Concentration of Revenues</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During the years ended December 31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">53.8%</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">52.1%</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">52.7%</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively, of the Company&#x2019;s revenues related to patients participating in the Medicare and Medicaid programs, collectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s management recognizes that revenues and receivables from government agencies are significant to the Company&#x2019;s operations, but it does not believe that there are significant credit risks associated with these government agencies. The Company&#x2019;s management does not believe that there are any other significant concentrations of r</font><font style="display: inline;">evenues from any particular paye</font><font style="display: inline;">r that would subject the Company to any significant credit risks in the collection of its accounts receivable.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Other Income </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 (&#x201C;ARRA&#x201D;) provides for incentive payments under the Medicare and Medicaid programs for certain hospitals and physician practices that demonstrate meaningful use of certified</font><font style="display: inline;"> electronic health record</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">(&#x201C;EHR&#x201D;) </font><font style="display: inline;">technology.&nbsp;&nbsp;These provisions of ARRA, collectively referred to as the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act (the &#x201C;HITECH Act&#x201D;), are intended to promote the adoption and meaningful use of interoperable health information technology and qualified EHR technology.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company accounts for EHR incentive payments in accordance with ASC 450-30, &#x201C;Gain Contingencies&#x201D; (&#x201C;ASC 450-30&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;In accordance with ASC 450-30, the Company recognizes a gain for EHR incentive payments when its eligible hospitals and physician practices have demonstrated meaningful use of certified EHR technology for the applicable period and when the cost report information for the full cost report year that determines the final calculation of the EHR incentive payment is available.&nbsp;&nbsp;The demonstration of meaningful use is based on meeting a series of objectives and varies among hospitals and physician practices, between the Medicare and Medicaid programs and within the Medicaid program from state to state.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, meeting the series of objectives in order to demonstrate meaningful use becomes progressively more stringent as its implementation is phased in through stages as outlined by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (&#x201C;CMS&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;EHR incentive payments are subject to audit and potential recoupment if it is determined that the Company&#x2019;s hospitals did not meet the applicable meaningful use standards required in connection with such incentive payments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Furthermore, EHR incentive payments are subject to retrospective adjustment because the cost report data upon which the payments are based are further subject to audit. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">For the years ended December 31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, the Company recognized </font><font style="display: inline;">$10.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$29.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$49.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in EHR incentive payments, respectively, under the Medicare and Medicaid HITECH Act programs, collectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;These payments are reflected separately in the accompanying consolidated statement of operations under the caption &#x201C;Other income&#x201D;.&nbsp;&nbsp;Amounts recognized as other income that the Company anticipates collecting in future periods, but that were uncollected as of the balance sheet date totaled approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$4.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$10.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million as of December 31, 2017 and 2016, respectively, and are included in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets under the caption &#x201C;Other current assets&#x201D;.&nbsp; </font>

The amount and timing of these expenditures does not directly correlate with the timing of the Company&#x2019;s receipt or recognition as other income of the EHR incentive payments. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;"> compliance has and will continue to result in additional costs including business process changes, professional services focused on successfully designing and implementing </font><font style="display: inline;">its</font><font style="display: inline;"> EHR solutions along with costs associated with the hardware and sof</font><font style="display: inline;">tware components of the project.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">H</font><font style="display: inline;">owever, </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;"> EHR incentive payments decreas</font><font style="display: inline;">ed and ultimately ended in 2017</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Cash and Cash Equivalents</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Cash and cash equivalents consist of cash on hand and marketable securities with original maturities of three months or less. The Company places its cash in financial institutions that are federally insured in limited amounts.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Inventories</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Inventories are stated at the lower of cost (first-in, first-out) or market and are comprised of purchased items. These inventory items are primarily operating supplies used in the direct or indirect treatment of patients. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Long-Lived Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;text-indent:13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Property and Equipment</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Purchases of property and equipment are recorded at cost. Property and equipment acquired in connection with business combinations are recorded at estimated fair value in accordance with the acquisition method of accounting as prescribed in ASC 805-10, &#x201C;Business Combinations&#x201D; (&#x201C;ASC 805-10&#x201D;). Routine maintenance and repairs are charged to expense as incurred. Expenditures that increase capacities or extend useful lives are capitalized. Fully depreciated assets are retained in property and equipment accounts until they are disposed of. Allocated interest on funds used to pay for the construction or purchase of major capital additions is included in the cost of each capital addition.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Depreciation is calculated by applying the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of buildings and improvements and equipment. Assets under capital and financing leases are generally amortized using the straight-line method over the shorter of the estimated useful life of the assets or life of the lease term, excluding any lease renewals, unless the lease renewals are reasonably assured.&nbsp;&nbsp;Capitalized internal-use software costs are amortized over their expected useful life, which is generally </font><font style="display: inline;">four</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.&nbsp;&nbsp;Useful lives are as follows:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 1pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:1pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse:collapse;width: 100.00%;margin-left:0pt;">
			<tr>
				<td valign="bottom" style="width:79.86%;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;background-color: #auto;height:1.00pt;padding:0pt;">
					<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;height:1.00pt;overflow:hidden;font-size: 1pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">The Company evaluates its long-lived assets for possible impairment whenever circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of the asset, or related group of assets, may not be recoverable from estimated future cash flows, in accordance with ASC 360-10</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">Impairment and Disposal of Long-Lived Assets</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D; (&#x201C;ASC 360-10&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;">. The Company&#x2019;s estimates of future cash flows are based on assumptions and projections it believes to be reasonable and supportable. The Company&#x2019;s assumptions take into account revenue and expense growth rates, </font><font style="display: inline;">patient volumes, changes in paye</font><font style="display: inline;">r mix and changes in l</font><font style="display: inline;">egislation and other paye</font><font style="display: inline;">r payment patterns. These assumptions vary by type of facility. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">During the year ended December 31, 2017, t</font><font style="display: inline;">he Company recognized impairment losses in the aggregate of </font><font style="display: inline;">$43.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$27.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million net of income taxes, or </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.67</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">loss </font><font style="display: inline;">per diluted share, to reduce the carrying amounts of certain long-lived assets at </font><font style="display: inline;">two</font><font style="display: inline;"> of its </font><font style="display: inline;">hospitals </font><font style="display: inline;">to their estimated fair values</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">which is included under the caption &#x201C;Other non-operating losses, net&#x201D; in the accompanying consolidated statements of income for the year ended December 31, 2017</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;As more fully discussed in Note 12, the majority of this impairment loss was recognized to adjust the estimated fair value of certain assets expected to be disposed </font><font style="display: inline;">upon completion of </font><font style="display: inline;">the construction of a replacement hospital</font><font style="display: inline;"> in Marquette, Michigan</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>

A portion of these charges related to the write-down of property and equipment to their estimated fair values. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">The fair values were estimated using the framework and hierarchy in ASC 820-10, as described in Note 1</font><font style="display: inline;">2</font><font style="display: inline;">, using a combination of the income, market, and cost approaches. Fair value estimates are derived using established market or replacement values of comparable assets and estimated future net cash flows expected to be generated by market participants The resulting fair values are considered nonrecurring Level 3 measurements, and are subject to change based on economic or market conditions, as well as future negotiations with interested parties.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Goodwill and Intangible Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company accounts for its acquisitions in accordance with ASC 805-10 using the acquisition method of accounting. Goodwill represents the excess of the cost of an acquired entity over the net amounts assigned to assets acquired and liabilities assumed. In accordance with ASC 350-10, &#x201C;Intangibles &#x2014; Goodwill and Other&#x201D; (&#x201C;ASC 350-10&#x201D;), goodwill and intangible assets with indefinite lives are reviewed by the Company at least annually for impairment. The Company&#x2019;s business comprises a single reporting unit for impairment test purposes. For the purposes of these analyses, the Company&#x2019;s estimates of fair value are based on a combination of the income approach, which estimates the fair value of the Company based on its future discounted cash flows, and the market approach, which estimates the fair value of the Company based on comparable market prices. During the years ended December 31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, the Company performed its annual impairment tests as of October 1 and did not incur an impairment charge.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s intangible assets relate to contract-based physician minimum revenue guarantees; non-competition agreements; certificates of need and certificates of need exemptions; and licenses, provider numbers, accreditations and other.&nbsp;&nbsp;Contract-based physician minimum revenue guarantees and non-competition agreements are amortized over the terms of the agreements. The certificates of need, certificates of need exemptions, licenses, provider numbers, accreditations and other have been determined to have indefinite lives and, accordingly, are not amortized. The Company&#x2019;s goodwill and intangible assets are further described in Note 5.</font>

		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"> Income Taxes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company accounts for income taxes using the asset and liability method. Under this method, deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates is recognized in income in the period that includes the enactment date. The Company assesses the likelihood that deferred tax assets will be recovered from future taxable income. To the extent the Company believes that recovery is not likely, a valuation allowance is established. To the extent the Company establishes a valuation allowance or increases this allowance, the Company must include an expense within the provision for income taxes in the consolidated statements of </font><font style="display: inline;">income</font><font style="display: inline;">. The Company classifies interest and penalties related to its tax positions as a component of income tax expense. Income taxes are further described in Note 7.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Point of Life Indemnity, Ltd. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company operates, with approval from the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority, a captive insurance company under the name Point of Life Indemnity, Ltd.&nbsp;&nbsp;Through this wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, the captive insurance company issues malpractice insurance policies to certain of the Company&#x2019;s employed physicians in addition to providing </font><font style="display: inline;">compensation deductible coverage.</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#FF0000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Fees charged to these employed physicians are eliminated in consolidation. Reserves for the Company&#x2019;s estimate of the related outstanding claims, including incurred but not reported losses, are actuarially determined and are included as a component of the Company&#x2019;s reserves for professional liability self-insurance claims, as further discussed in this note.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Reserves for Self-Insurance Claims</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Given the nature of the Company&#x2019;s operating environment, it is subject to potential professional liability claims, employee workers&#x2019; compensation claims and other claims. To mitigate a portion of this risk, the Company maintains insurance for individual professional liability claims and employee workers&#x2019; compensation claims exceeding self-insured retention and deductible levels. The Company&#x2019;s self-insured retention level for professional liability claims is </font><font style="display: inline;">$5.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million per claim at December 31, 2017 with a </font><font style="display: inline;">$5.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million inner aggregate per claim.&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Additionally, the Company participates in state specific professional liability programs in Indiana, Kansas,</font><font style="display: inline;"> New Mexico,</font><font style="display: inline;"> Pennsylvania and Wisconsin.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;T</font><font style="display: inline;">he Company&#x2019;s deductible for workers&#x2019; compensation claims is </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million per claim in all states in which it operates except for Wyoming. The Company participates in a state specific program in Wyoming for its workers&#x2019; compensation claims arising in this state.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s self-insured retention and deductible levels are evaluated annually as a part of its insur</font><font style="display: inline;">ance program&#x2019;s renewal process.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s reserves for self-insurance and deductible claims reflect the current estimate of all outstanding losses, including incurred but not reported losses, based upon actuarial calculations as of the balance sheet date. The loss estimates included in the actuarial calculations may change in the future based upon updated facts and circumstances. The Company&#x2019;s expense for self-insurance and deductible claims coverage each year includes: the actuarially determined estimate of losses for the current year, including claims incurred but not reported; the change in the estimate of losses for prior years based upon actual claims development experience as compared to prior actuarial projections; the insurance premiums for losses in excess of the Company&#x2019;s self-insured retention and deductible levels; the administrative costs of the insurance program; and interest expense related to the discounted portion of the liability. The Company&#x2019;s expense for self-insurance and deductible claims was approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$33.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$76.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$56.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million for the years ended December 31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively. The Company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;s insurance expenses were lower</font><font style="display: inline;"> for the year ended December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;"> as a result of </font><font style="display: inline;">favorable claims development under </font><font style="display: inline;">its </font><font style="display: inline;">self-insured professional liability program</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> The Company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;s insurance expenses were higher </font><font style="display: inline;">for the year ended December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6 as a result of </font><font style="display: inline;">recording an accrual for loss contingencies</font><font style="display: inline;"> of </font><font style="display: inline;">$24.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;"> for cardiology-related legal proceedings</font><font style="display: inline;">, which are</font><font style="display: inline;"> described further in Note 12.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s reserves for professional liability claims are based upon quarterly actuarial calculations. The Company&#x2019;s reserves for employee workers&#x2019; compensation claims are based upon semi-annual actuarial calculations. These reserve calculations consider historical claims data, demographic considerations, severity factors and other actuarial assumptions, which are discounted to present value. The Company&#x2019;s reserves for self-insured claims have been discounted to their present value using a discount rate of </font><font style="display: inline;">1.42%</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">1.31%</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">1.35%</font><font style="display: inline;"> at December 31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively. The Company&#x2019;s management selects a discount rate by considering a risk-free interest rate that corresponds to the period when the self-insured claims are incurred and projected to be paid.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">Professional and general liability claims are typically resolved over an extended period of time, often as long as </font><font style="display: inline;">five</font><font style="display: inline;"> years or more, while workers&#x2019; compensation claims are typically resolved in </font><font style="display: inline;">one</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">two</font><font style="display: inline;"> years. Accordingly, the Company&#x2019;s reserves for self-insured claims, comprised of estimated indemnity and expense payments related to reported events and incurred but not reported events as of the end of the period, include both a current and long-term component. The current portion of the Company&#x2019;s reserves for self-insured claims is included under the caption &#x201C;Other current liabilities&#x201D; and the long-term portion is included under the caption &#x201C;Long-term portion of reserves for self-insurance claims&#x201D; in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.</font>

		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The combination of changing conditions and the extended time required for claim resolution results in a loss estimation process that requires actuarial skill and the application of judgment, and such estimates require periodic revision. As a result of the variety of factors that must be considered, there is a risk that actual incurred losses may develop differently from estimates. The results of the Company&#x2019;s quarterly and semi-annual actuarial calculations resulted in changes to its reserves for self-insured claims for prior years. As a result, for the years ended December 31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, the Company&#x2019;s related self-insured claims expense decreased by </font><font style="display: inline;">$32.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$31.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$21.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, which increased net income by approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$20.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$19.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$13.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, or </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.50</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">$0.45</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.29</font><font style="display: inline;"> per diluted share, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Self-Insured Medical Benefits</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company is self-insured for substantially all of the medical expenses and benefits of its employees. The reserve for medical benefits primarily reflects the current estimate of incurred but not reported losses based upon an annual actuarial calculation as of the balance sheet date. The undiscounted reserve for self-insured medical benefits was </font><font style="display: inline;">$44.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;m</font><font style="display: inline;">illion and </font><font style="display: inline;">$39.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million at December 31, 2017 and 2016, respectively, and is included in the Company&#x2019;s accompanying consolidated balance sheets under the caption &#x201C;Other current liabilities&#x201D;.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Noncontrolling Interests and Redeemable Noncontrolling Interests</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Noncontrolling interests represent the portion of equity in a subsidiary not attributable, directly or indirectly, to a parent. The Company&#x2019;s accompanying consolidated financial statements include all assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses at their consolidated amounts, which include the amounts attributable to the Company and the noncontrolling interest. The Company recognizes as a separate component of equity and earnings on the portion of income or loss attributable to noncontrolling interests based on the portion of the entity not owned by the Company.</font>
		</p>
