		<p style="margin:12pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Segment Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 10pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">provides healthcare services primarily through its ownership and operation of community hospitals and regional health systems, certain of which provide related healthcare services through </font><font style="display: inline;">physician practices, outpatient centers, and post-acute facilities</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> Accordingly, the Company has</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">one</font><font style="display: inline;"> operating segment, healthcare services, for segment reporting purposes in accordance with ASC 280-10, &#x201C;S</font><font style="display: inline;">egment Reporting&#x201D;. Additionally, the Company has </font><font style="display: inline;">one</font><font style="display: inline;"> reporting unit for goodwill impairment testing in accordance with </font><font style="display: inline;">ASC 350-10.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Stock-Based Compensation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company issues stock-based awards to key employees and directors under various stockholder-approved stock-based compensation plans, as further described in Note </font><font style="display: inline;">10</font><font style="display: inline;">. The Company accounts for its stock-based awards in accordance with the provisions of ASC 718-10 &#x201C;Compensation&nbsp;&#x2014;&nbsp;Stock Compensation&#x201D;, (&#x201C;ASC 718-10&#x201D;). In accordance with ASC 718-10, the Company recognizes compensation expense over each of the stock-based award&#x2019;s requisite service period based on the estimated grant date fair value of each stock-based award.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Deferred Cash Awards</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company grants deferred cash awards to certain employees that are subject to continuing service requirements and a ratable vesting term of </font><font style="display: inline;">three</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company recognizes compensation expense for these awards over their requisite service period.&nbsp;&nbsp;For the years ended December 31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, expense related to the Company&#x2019;s deferred cash awards was approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$10.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$10.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$8.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2017, there was </font><font style="display: inline;">$13.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;m</font><font style="display: inline;">illion of total estimated unrecognized compensation costs related to deferred cash awards arrangements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company expects to recognize this cost over a weighted average period of </font><font style="display: inline;">1.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.</font>
		</p>

The Company&#x2019;s expense related to its defined contribution plan</font><font style="display: inline;">(</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;">)</font><font style="display: inline;"> was </font><font style="display: inline;">$27.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$27.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$23.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million for the years ended December 31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively.</font>

		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Defined Benefit Pension Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company maintain</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> certain defined benefit pension plans for a small population of the Company&#x2019;s employees. The Company accounts for its defined benefit pension plans in accordance with ASC 715-30 &#x201C;Compensation &#x2013; Defined Benefit Plans&#x201D;, (&#x201C;ASC 715-30&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;In accordance with ASC 715-30, the Company recognizes the unfunded liability of its defined benefit pension plans in the Company&#x2019;s consolidated balance sheets and unrecognized gains (losses) and prior service credits (costs) as changes in other comprehensive income (loss).&nbsp;&nbsp;The measurement date of the defined benefit pension plans&#x2019; assets and liabilities coincides with the Company&#x2019;s year-end.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s pension benefit obligation is measured using actuarial calculations that incorporate discount rates, rate of compensation increases, when applicable, expected long-term returns on plan assets and consider expected age of retirement and mortality. The Company&#x2019;s defined benefit pension plans ar</font><font style="display: inline;">e described further in Note 11.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">EPS is based on the weighted average number of common shares outstanding and the effect of stock options, other stock-based awards</font><font style="display: inline;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;"> common stock warrants, when dilutive. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 20.9pt 12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Adoption of Recently Issued Accounting Standards</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">ASU 2016-9, &#x201C;Compensation &#x2013; Stock Compensation:&nbsp;&nbsp;Improvements to Employee Share-Based Payment Accounting&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In March 2016, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#x201C;FASB&#x201D;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#x201C;ASU&#x201D;) 2016-9 &#x201C;Compensation &#x2013; Stock Compensation:&nbsp;&nbsp;Improvements to Employee Share-Based Payment Accounting&#x201D; (&#x201C;ASU 2016-9&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2016-9 changes certain aspects of accounting for share-based payment awards to employees, including the accounting for income taxes, application of estimated rates of forfeiture and statutory tax withholding requirements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company prospectively adopted the provisions of ASU 2016-9 during the first quarter of 2017.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In accordance with ASU 2016-9, differences in the amount of compensation expense recognized for accounting purposes and tax purposes are recognized as an excess tax benefit or deficiency through the provision for income taxes.&nbsp; Prior to the adoption of ASU 2016-9, the Company recognized these differences through capital in excess of par value.&nbsp; During the year ended December 31, 2017, the Company recognized a reduction to its provision for income taxes of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$2.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million as a result of compensation expense for tax purposes upon vesting or settlement of certain share-based awards exceeding the amount of compensation expense that had previously been recognized for accounting purposes for these same share-based awards.&nbsp; Additionally, as part of the Company&#x2019;s adoption of the provisions of ASU 2016-9, the Company elected to continue to apply an estimated rate of forfeiture to its compensation expense for share-based awards.&nbsp; Finally, ASU 2016-9 allows an employer to withhold employee shares upon vesting up to maximum statutory tax rates without causing an award to be classified as a liability.&nbsp; The Company made certain modifications to its share-based award plans and certain awards under those plans in order to accommodate and administer this additional provision of ASU 2016-9.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 20.9pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:12pt 20.9pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 20.9pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Accounting Standards Not Yet Adopted</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">ASU 2014-9, &#x201C;Revenue from Contracts with Customers</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In May 2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-9, &#x201C;Revenue from Contracts with Customers&#x201D;, along with subsequent amendments, updates and an extension of the effective date (collectively, the &#x201C;New Revenue Standard&#x201D;), which supersedes most existing revenue recognition guidance, including industry-specific healthcare guidance.&nbsp; The New Revenue Standard provides for a single comprehensive principles-based standard for the recognition of revenue across all industries through the application of the following five-step process:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Step 1: Identify the contract(s) with a customer. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Step 2: Identify the performance obligations in the contract. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Step 3: Determine the transaction price. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Step 4: Allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Step 5: Recognize revenue when (or as) the entity satisfies a performance obligation.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">This five-step process will require significant management judgment in addition to changing the way many companies recognize revenue in their financial statements.&nbsp; Additionally, and among other provisions, the New Revenue Standard requires expanded quantitative and qualitative disclosures, including disclosure about the nature, amount, timing and uncertainty of revenue.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The provisions of the New Revenue Standard are effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2017, including interim periods within those years by applying either the full retrospective method or the cumulative catch-up transition method.&nbsp; The full retrospective method requires application of the provisions of the New Revenue Standard for all periods presented while the cumulative catch-up transition method requires the application of the provisions of the New Revenue Standard as of the date of adoption with the cumulative effect of the retrospective application of the provisions as an adjustment through retained earnings.&nbsp; Currently, the Company anticipates adopting the provisions of the New Revenue Standard using the </font><font style="display: inline;">cumulative catch-up transition</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">method</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">ASU 2016-2, &#x201C;Leases&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In February 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-2 &#x201C;Leases&#x201D; (&#x201C;ASU 2016-2&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2016-2 requires the rights and obligations arising from lease contracts, including existing and new arrangements, to be recognized as assets and liabilities on the balance sheet.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2016-2 is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2018, including interim periods within those years.&nbsp;&nbsp;Early adoption is permitted. The Company anticipates that the adoption of ASU 2016-2 will result in an increase in both total assets and total liabilities reflected on the Company&#x2019;s balance sheets. The Company is still evaluating the impact that the adoption of this standard will have on its policies, procedures, financial disc</font><font style="display: inline;">losures, and control framework.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Note 4. In-Home Healthcare Partnership</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Effective January 1, 2017, the Company entered into a joint venture agreement with a wholly-owned subsidiary of LHC Group, Inc. (&#x201C;LHC&#x201D;) to form In-Home Healthcare Partnership (&#x201C;IHHP&#x201D;), the purpose of which is to own and operate the Company&#x2019;s home health agencies and hospices and certain of LHC&#x2019;s home health agencies and hospices, leveraging the combined expertise of the Company and LHC to enhance home health and hospice services in the communities served by the Company&#x2019;s hospitals.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company accounts for its ownership interest in IHHP as an equity method investment in accordance with ASC 323-10, &#x201C;Investments &#x2013; Equity Method and Joint Ventures&#x201D;.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During the year ended December 31, 2017, ownership and management of </font><font style="display: inline;">19</font><font style="display: inline;"> of the Company&#x2019;s home health agencies and </font><font style="display: inline;">10</font><font style="display: inline;"> of the Company&#x2019;s hospices have been transferred to IHHP over the course of </font><font style="display: inline;">three</font><font style="display: inline;"> phases.&nbsp;&nbsp;The transfer of </font><font style="display: inline;">one</font><font style="display: inline;"> additional home health agency </font><font style="display: inline;">owned by the Company</font><font style="display: inline;"> is scheduled to be completed in a final phase during the first quarter of 2018, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.&nbsp;&nbsp;In connection with the three completed phases, the Company has transferred assets primarily comprised of accounts receivable and allocated goodwill in exchange for cash, and recognized aggregate gains of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$28.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$14.</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million when adjusted for the impact of income taxes, or </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.3</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;"> per diluted share, which is included under the capt</font><font style="display: inline;">ion &#x201C;Other non-operating</font><font style="display: inline;"> losses, net&#x201D; in the accompanying consolidated statements of </font><font style="display: inline;">income</font><font style="display: inline;"> for the year ended December 31, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Included in the net gains recognized during the year ended December 31, 2017 are write-offs of allocated goodwill, which were not fully deductible for income tax purposes.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">As a result, the nondeductible portion of the goodwill write-offs contributed to an increase in the Company&#x2019;s consolidated effective tax rate for the year ended December 31, 2017.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; 			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Contract-Based Physician Minimum Revenue Guarantees</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has committed to provide certain financial assistance pursuant to recruiting agreements, or &#x201C;physician minimum revenue guarantees,&#x201D; with various physicians practicing in the communities it serves. In consideration for a physician relocating to one of its communities and agreeing to engage in private practice for the benefit of the respective community, the Company may advance certain amounts of money to a physician to assist in establishing his or her practice.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company accounts for its physician minimum revenue guarantees in accordance with the provisions of ASC 460-10, &#x201C;Guarantees&#x201D; (&#x201C;ASC 460-10&#x201D;). In accordance with ASC 460-10, the Company records a contract-based intangible asset and a related guarantee liability for new physician minimum revenue guarantees. The contract-based intangible asset is amortized as a component of other operating expenses, in the accompanying consolidated statements of </font><font style="display: inline;">income</font><font style="display: inline;">, over the period of the physician contract, which typically ranges from </font><font style="display: inline;">four</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">five</font><font style="display: inline;"> years. As of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">, the Company&#x2019;s liability for contract-based physician minimum revenue guarantees was </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">6.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$8.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively. These amounts are included as a current liability under the caption &#x201C;Other current liabilities&#x201D; in the Company&#x2019;s accompanying consolidated balance sheets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 20.9pt 11pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Senior Credit Agreement</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:8pt 0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Terms</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Senior Credit Agreement, which was issued effective June 10, 2016 and matures on June 10, 2021 </font><font style="display: inline;">provides for the </font><font style="display: inline;">$700.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million Term Facility </font><font style="display: inline;">and </font><font style="display: inline;">a</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;$</font><font style="display: inline;">600.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;"> senior secured revolving credit facility (the</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">Revolving Facility</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;">).</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The Term Facility requires scheduled quarterly repayments in an amount equal to 2.5% per annum for each of the first, second and third years and 5.0% per annum for the fourth year and first three quarters of the fifth year, with the balance due at maturity.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Additionally, the Term Facility </font><font style="display: inline;">is</font><font style="display: inline;"> subject to mandatory prepayments based on excess cash flow, as well as upon the occurrence of certain other events, as specifically described in the Senior Credit Agreement. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Senior Credit Agreement is guaranteed, on a senior basis, by</font><font style="display: inline;"> certain of the Company&#x2019;s subsidiaries</font><font style="display: inline;">. The Senior Credit Agreement is secured by collateral consisting of a perfected first priority lien on, and pledge of, all of the capital stock and intercompany notes issued by the Company&#x2019;s subsidiaries and owned by the Company and each guarantor, subject to certain exceptions.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:8pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Letters of Credit and Availability</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:8pt 0pt;text-indent:13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Revolving Facility may be utilized for letters of credit and swingline loans up to a maximum of $</font><font style="display: inline;">100.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and $</font><font style="display: inline;">50.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Issued letters of credit and outstanding swingline loans reduce the amounts available for borrowing under the Revolving Facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">, the Company had </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">20.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in letters of credit outstanding that were related to the self-insured retention level of its general and professional liability insurance and workers&#x2019; compensation programs as security for payment of claims.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Throughout </font><font style="display: inline;">2017, the Company </font><font style="display: inline;">borrowed</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">subsequently </font><font style="display: inline;">repaid </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">205.0</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">million under the Revolving Facility for general corporate purposes. </font><font style="display: inline;">Under the terms of the Senior Credit Agreement, amounts available for borrowing under the Revolving Facility were </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">580.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million as of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:8pt 0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Senior Credit Agreement may, subject to certain conditions and to receipt of commitments from new or existing lenders, be increased up to a total of (i) $</font><font style="display: inline;">800.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and (ii) an amount such that, after giving pro forma effect to such increase and to the use of proceeds therefrom, the Company&#x2019;s secured leverage ratio does not exceed </font><font style="display: inline;">3.50</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00; provided that no lender is obligated to participate in any such increase. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:8pt 0pt 8pt 13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Interest Rates</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:8pt 0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Interest on the outstanding borrowings under the Senior Credit Agreement is payable at the Company&#x2019;s option at either an adjusted London Interbank Offer Rate (&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">LIBOR</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;) or an adjusted base rate plus an applicable margin.&nbsp;&nbsp;The applicable margin under the Senior Credit Agreement ranges from </font><font style="display: inline;">1.50</font><font style="display: inline;">% to </font><font style="display: inline;">2.00</font><font style="display: inline;">% for LIBOR loans and from </font><font style="display: inline;">0.50</font><font style="display: inline;">% to </font><font style="display: inline;">1.00</font><font style="display: inline;">% for adjusted base rate loans based on the Company&#x2019;s total leverage ratio, calculated in accordance with the Senior Credit Agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">, the </font><font style="display: inline;">applicable annual interest rate</font><font style="display: inline;"> under the Term Facility </font><font style="display: inline;">was</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">3.32</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font><font style="display: inline;">, which w</font><font style="display: inline;">as</font><font style="display: inline;"> based on the </font><font style="display: inline;">30-day adjusted LIBOR of 1.57</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;p</font><font style="display: inline;">lus the applicable margin</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:8pt 0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Covenants</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Senior Credit Agreement requires the Company to satisfy a maximum total leverage ratio not to exceed </font><font style="display: inline;">5.00</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00 through June 30, 2018 with a step-down to </font><font style="display: inline;">4.50</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00 through the remaining term and as calculated on a trailing four quarter basis.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company was in compliance with this covenant as of December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;"> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (the &#x201C;Tax Act&#x2019;) was signed into law on December 22, 2017. The Tax Act significantly revises the U.S. corporate income tax by, among other things, lowering the statutory corporate tax rate from </font><font style="display: inline;">35%</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">21%</font><font style="display: inline;"> and eliminating certain deductions. The Tax Act also enhanced and extended through 2026 the option to claim accelerated depreciation deductions on qualified property. </font><font style="display: inline;">Due to the timing of the enactment and the complexity involved in applying the provisions of the Tax Act</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the Company has</font><font style="display: inline;"> not completed its determination of the accounting implications of the Tax Act on its income tax accruals. However, the Company has reasonably estimated the effects of the Tax Act on its existing deferred tax assets and liabilities and recognized a provisional benefit for income taxes of </font><font style="display: inline;">$18.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, or </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.44</font><font style="display: inline;"> per diluted share, for the year ended December 31, 2017. This amount is primarily comprised of the remeasurement of federal net deferred tax assets and liabilities resulting from the permanent reduction in the U.S. statutory corporate tax rate to 21% from 35%. &nbsp;As the Company completes its analysis of the Tax Act, including the collection of data and interpretation of any additional guidance issued by the U.S. Treasury Department, the Internal Revenue Service (&#x201C;IRS&#x201D;), and other standard-setting bodies, </font><font style="display: inline;">it </font><font style="display: inline;">may make adjustments to the provisional amounts. Those adjustments may materially impact the Company&#x2019;s provision for income taxes in the period in which the adjustments are made.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The increase in the valuation allowance during the year ended December 31, 2017 was primarily the result of state net operating loss carry forwards that management believes, after evaluation of the four sources of income pursuant to ASC 740, may not be fully utilized because of the uncertainty regarding the Company&#x2019;s ability to generate taxable income in certain separate return filing states. Various subsidiaries have separate return state net operating loss carry forwards in the aggregate of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">1.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> billion, </font><font style="display: inline;">primarily in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia, and West Virginia, with expiration dates through the year </font><font style="display: inline;">2037</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Note </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">9</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">. Stockholders&#x2019; Equity</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;line-height:95%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Preferred Stock</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation provides that up to </font><font style="display: inline;">10,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares of preferred stock may be issued, of which </font><font style="display: inline;">90,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares have been designated as Series A Junior Participating Preferred Stock, par value $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.01</font><font style="display: inline;"> per share (&#x201C;Series A Preferred Stock&#x201D;). The Board of Directors has the authority to issue preferred stock in one or more series and to fix for each series the voting powers (full, limited or none), and the designations, preferences and relative participating, optional or other special rights and qualifications, limitations or restrictions on the stock and the number of shares constituting any series and the designations of this series, without any further vote or action by the stockholders. Because the terms of the preferred stock may be fixed by the Board of Directors without stockholder action, the preferred stock could be issued quickly with terms calculated to defeat a proposed takeover or to make the removal of the Company&#x2019;s management more difficult.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;line-height:95%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Preferred Stock Purchase Rights</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On September 21, 2015, the Company entered into Amendment No. 1 (the &#x201C;Amendment&#x201D;) to the Amended and Restated Rights Agreement (the &#x201C;Rights Agreement&#x201D;), dated as of February 25, 2009, between the Company and American Stock Transfer &amp; Trust Company, LLC, as rights agent. The Amendment accelerated the expiration date of the preferred stock purchase rights (the &#x201C;Rights&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">from February 25, 2019 to September 21, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, on September 21, 2015, the Rights Agreement was terminated and all of the Rights distributed to holders of the Company&#x2019;s common stock pursuant to the Rights Agreement expired.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt;line-height:95%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Common Stock</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Holders of the Company&#x2019;s common stock are entitled to </font><font style="display: inline;">one</font><font style="display: inline;"> vote for each share held of record on all matters on which stockholders may vote. There are no preemptive, conversion, redemption or sinking fund provisions applicable to shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock. In the event of liquidation, dissolution or winding up, holders of the Company&#x2019;s common stock are entitled to share ratably in the assets available for distribution, subject to any prior rights of any holders of preferred stock then outstanding. Delaware law prohibits the Company from paying any dividends unless it has capital surplus or net profits available for this purpose. In addition, </font><font style="display: inline;">certain restrictions imposed by the Company&#x2019;s various debt instruments may limit the</font><font style="display: inline;"> Company&#x2019;s ability to pay dividends.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Common Stock in Treasury and Repurchases of Common Stock</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

Other comprehensive income </font><font style="display: inline;">(loss) </font><font style="display: inline;">refers to revenues, expenses, gains and losses that in accordance with ASC 220-10 &#x201C;Comprehensive Income,&#x201D; are recorded as an element of stockholders&#x2019; equity but are excluded from net income.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Company issues stock-based awards, including stock options and other stock-based awards (nonvested stock, restricted stock, restricted stock units and performance shares) to certain officers, employees and non-employee directors in accordance with th</font><font style="display: inline;">e Company&#x2019;s various stockholder-</font><font style="display: inline;">approved stock-based compensation plans. The Company accounts for its stock-based awards in accordance with the provisions of ASC 718-10 and accordingly recognizes compensation expense over each of the stock-based award&#x2019;s requisite service period based on the estimated grant date fair value. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Stockholder-</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Approved Stock-Based Compensation Plans</font>

		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Effective June 4, 2013, upon the approval of the Company&#x2019;s stockholders, the Company replaced the Amended and Restated 1998 Long-Term Incentive Plan (the &#x201C;1998 LTIP&#x201D;) and Amended and Restated Outside Directors Stock and Incentive Compensation Plan (the &#x201C;ODSICP&#x201D;) with the 2013 Long-Term Incentive Plan, which was amended and restated effective June 6, 2017 (the &#x201C;2013 LTIP&#x201D;), a combined plan covering all of the Company&#x2019;s employees and non-employee directors.&nbsp;&nbsp;No shares remain available for grant under the 1998 LTIP or the ODSICP.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Notwithstanding the specific grant vesting requirements, award agreements under the 2013 LTIP and the 1998 LTIP may provide for accelerated vesting in certain circumstances.&nbsp; Generally, award agreements provide for full vesting upon the death or disability of the participant.&nbsp; Some award agreements also provide for partial or full vesting upon involuntary termination of employment, provided that if the award is performance-based then the accelerated vesting would occur only if the performance goals are attained.</font>

Options to purchase shares granted to the Company&#x2019;s officers and employees become ratably exercisable beginning </font><font style="display: inline;">one</font><font style="display: inline;"> year from the date of </font><font style="display: inline;">grant to either </font><font style="display: inline;">three</font><font style="display: inline;"> or </font><font style="display: inline;">four</font><font style="display: inline;"> yea</font><font style="display: inline;">rs after the date of grant and expire </font><font style="display: inline;">ten</font><font style="display: inline;"> years from the date of grant.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Valuation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 5pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company estimated the fair value of stock options granted using a binomial lattice option valuation model and a single option award approach.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company uses a binomial lattice option valuation model because it considers characteristics of fair value option pricing, such as an option&#x2019;s contractual term and the probability of exercise before the end of the contractual term.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the complications surrounding the expected term of an option are material, as indicated in ASC 718-10.&nbsp;&nbsp;Given the Company&#x2019;s relatively large pool of unexercised options, the Company believes a binomial lattice option valuation model that specifically addresses this fact and models a full term of exercises is the most appropriate and reliable means of valuing its stock options.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is amortizing the fair value on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period of the awards, which is the vesting period of three or four years.&nbsp;&nbsp;The stock options vest at </font><font style="display: inline;">either </font><font style="display: inline;">33.3%</font><font style="display: inline;"> or </font><font style="display: inline;">25.0%</font><font style="display: inline;"> on each grant anniversary date over </font><font style="display: inline;">three</font><font style="display: inline;"> or </font><font style="display: inline;">four</font><font style="display: inline;"> years</font><font style="display: inline;"> of continued employment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The following table shows the weighted average assumptions the Company used to develop the fair value estimates under its </font><font style="display: inline;">lattice</font><font style="display: inline;"> option valuation model and the resulting estimates of weighted-average fair value per share of stock options granted during the years ended December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">:</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:12pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Population Stratification</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In accordance with ASC 718-10, a company should aggregate individual awards into relatively homogeneous groups with respect to exercise and post-vesting employment behaviors for the purpose of refining the expected term assumption, regardless of the valuation technique used to estimate the fair value. In addition, ASC 718-10 indicates that a company may generally make a reasonable fair value estimate with as few as one or two groupings. The Company has determined that a single employee population group is appropriate based on an analysis of the Company&#x2019;s historical exercise patterns.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt 13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Expected Volatility</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:3pt 4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Volatility is a measure of the tendency of investment returns to vary around a long-term average rate. Historical volatility is an appropriate starting point for setting this assumption in accordance with ASC 718-10. According to ASC 718-10, companies should also consider how future experience may differ from the past. This may require using other factors to adjust historical volatility, such as implied volatility, peer-group volatility and the range and mean-reversion of volatility estimates over various historical periods. ASC 718-10 acknowledges that there is likely to be a range of reasonable estimates for volatility. In addition, ASC 718-10 requires that if a best estimate cannot be made, management should use the mid-point in the range of reasonable estimates for volatility. The Company estimates the volatility of its common stock at the date of grant based on both historical volatility and implied volatility from traded options of its common stock, consistent with ASC 718-10.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Risk-Free Interest Rate</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Lattice models require risk-free interest rates for all potential times of exercise obtained by using a grant-date yield curve. A lattice model would, therefore, require the yield curve for the entire time period during which employees might exercise their options. The Company bases the risk-free rate on the implied yield in effect at the time of option grant on U.S. Treasury zero-coupon issues with equivalent remaining terms.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 12pt 13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Expected Dividends</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has never paid any cash dividends on its common stock and does not anticipate paying any cash dividends in the foreseeable future. Accordingly, the Company uses an expected dividend yield of </font><font style="display: inline;">zero</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 12pt 13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Pre-Vesting Forfeitures</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Pre-vesting forfeitures do not affect the fair value calculation, but they affect the expense calculation. ASC 718-10 requires the Company to estimate pre-vesting forfeitures at the time of grant and revise those estimates in subsequent periods if actual forfeitures differ from those estimates. The Company uses historical data to estimate pre-vesting forfeitures and record share-based compensation expense only for those awards that are expected to vest.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company applies a dynamic forfeiture rate methodology over the vesting period of the award. The dynamic forfeiture rate methodology incorporates the lapse of time into the resulting expense calculation and results in a forfeiture rate that diminishes as the granted awards approach its vest date. Accordingly, the dynamic forfeiture rate methodology results in a more consistent stock-based compensation expense calculation over the vesting period of the award.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:13.7pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Post-Vesting Cancellations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Post-vesting cancellations include vested options that are cancelled, exercised or expire unexercised. Lattice models treat post-vesting cancellations and voluntary early exercise behavior as two separate assumptions. The Company uses historical data to estimate post-vesting cancellations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 12pt 13.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Expected Term</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">ASC 718-10 calls for an extinguishment calculation, dependent upon how long a granted option remains outstanding before it is fully extinguished. While extinguishment may result from exercise, it can also result from post-vesting cancellation or expiration at the contractual term. Expected term is an output in lattice models so the Company does not</font><font style="display: inline;"> have to determine this amount.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Defined Benefit Pension Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:15.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In connection with its acquisition of Marquette </font><font style="display: inline;">General Health System (&#x201C;Marquette General&#x201D;) in </font><font style="display: inline;">2012</font><font style="display: inline;">, the Company acquired certain assets and assumed certain liabilities associated with the benefits in the seller&#x2019;s defined benefit pension plan of certain employees covered by a collective bargaining agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has established a separate defined benefit pension plan (the &#x201C;Marquette Pension Plan&#x201D;) to facilitate its administration of the assumed portion of the seller&#x2019;s defined benefit pension plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, in connection with its acquisition of Bell Hospital (&#x201C;Bell&#x201D;) in </font><font style="display: inline;">2013</font><font style="display: inline;">, the</font><font style="display: inline;"> Company assumed sponsorship of Bell&#x2019;s defined benefit pension plan, which provides benefits to certain non-union employees (the &#x201C;Bell Pension Plan&#x201D; and, collectively with the Marquette Pensio</font><font style="display: inline;">n Plan, the &#x201C;Pension Plans&#x201D;).&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Both Pension Plans are closed to new participants.&nbsp;&nbsp;Participants in the Marquette Pension Plan are required to make annual contributions totaling </font><font style="display: inline;">6%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of annual compensation to the Marquette Pension Plan to continue accruing benefits.&nbsp;&nbsp;Participants in the Bell Pension Plan stopped accruing benefits when the Bell Pension Plan was frozen by Bell, effective October 31, 2005, prior to its assumption by the Company. The Company makes contributions to the Pension Plans sufficient to meet its minimum funding requirements as prescribed by the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Plan Assets </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The investment policy for the Pension Plans has been formulated to achieve a risk adjusted return that balances the need for asset growth against the risk of significant fluctuations in asset prices and the need for significant contributions from the Compa</font><font style="display: inline;">ny. </font><font style="display: inline;">On a quarterly basis, or more frequently as necessary, the current risk levels, asset performance and expected return on assets are reviewed and evaluated against goals and targets by a committee appointed to oversee investment of the Pension Plans&#x2019; assets (the &#x201C;Investment Committee&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Investment Committee strives to maintain a balance between risk and return through the use of modern portfolio theory methods, in conjunction with Monte Carlo modeling to evaluate the behavior of the portfolio under different scenarios. </font><font style="display: inline;">At December 31, 2017, the Pension Plans&#x2019; investments include a balance of mutual funds and money market funds in order </font><font style="display: inline;">to achieve an overall rate of return that minimizes the need for additional employer contributions.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company measures the fair value of its Pension Plans&#x2019; assets in accordance with ASC 820-10.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASC 820-10 establishes a framework for measuring fair value and establishes a three-tier fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs used in measuring fair value. The tiers are as follows: </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 1 - defined as observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 82.1pt;text-indent: -46.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 2 - defined as inputs other than quoted prices in active markets that are either directly or indirectly observable; and</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 74.15pt;text-indent: -38.15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 3 - defined as unobservable inputs in which little or no market data exists, therefore req</font><font style="display: inline;">uiring an entity to develop its </font><font style="display: inline;">own assumptions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Pension Plans&#x2019; investments in mutual funds are valued at the net asset value (&#x201C;NAV&#x201D;) of shares reported in the active market in which the funds are traded.&nbsp;&nbsp;Because quoted prices are available for mutual funds and the markets in which they are traded are generally considered active, the Company has classified each of them as a Level 1 investment.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The Pension Plans&#x2019; i</font><font style="display: inline;">nvestments in money market funds are valued at</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">quoted prices in markets that are not active by a combination of inputs, including but not limited to dealer quotes who are market makers in the underlying funds and other directly and indirectly observable inputs. </font><font style="display: inline;">Because the inputs used to value money market funds are either directly or indirectly observable</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> but </font><font style="display: inline;">are not</font><font style="display: inline;"> quoted prices in active markets, the Company has classified these assets as Level 2 investments.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Multiemployer Pension Plan</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As a result of the acquisition of Bell effective December 1, 2013, the Company became obligated to contribute to a multiemployer pension plan on behalf of certain employees covered by collective bargaining agreements, in accordance with the terms of such collective bargaining agreements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s contributions to the multiemployer pension plan are determined based on the terms of the applicable collective bargaining agreements.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Multiemployer plans are different from single-employer plans because assets contributed to the multiemployer plan by one employer may be used to provide benefits to employees of other participating employers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also, if a participating employer stops contributing to the plan, the unfunded obligations of the plan may be borne by the remaining participating employers.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the Company stops participating in the multiemployer plan, the Company may be required to pay a withdrawal liability based on its portion of the unfunded status of the plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;Currently, the Company does not anticipate ending its participation in this plan.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:15.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Note 1</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">. Commitments and Contingencies</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 20.9pt 5pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Legal Proceedings and General Liability </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Claims&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Healthcare facilities are, from time to time, subject to claims and suits arising in the ordinary course of business, including claims for damages for personal injuries, medical malpractice, breach of contracts, wrongful restriction of or interference with physicians&#x2019; staff privileges and employment related claims. In certain of these actions, plaintiffs request payment for damages, including punitive damages that may not be covered by insurance.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In addition, healthcare facilities are subject to the regulation and oversight of various state and federal governmental agencies. Further, under the federal False Claims Act, private parties have the right to bring qui tam, or &#x201C;whistleblower,&#x201D; suits against healthcare facilities that submit false claims for payments to, or improperly retain identified over</font><font style="display: inline;">payments from, governmental paye</font><font style="display: inline;">rs. Some states have adopted similar state whistleblower and false claims provisions. </font><font style="display: inline;">These qui tam or &#x201C;whistleblower&#x201D; actions initiated under the civil False Claims Act may be pending but placed under seal by the court to comply with the False Claims Act&#x2019;s requirements for filing such suits. As a result, they could be proceeding without the Company&#x2019;s knowledge. If a provider is found to be liable under the federal False Claims Act, the provider may be required to pay up to three times the actual damages sustained by the government plus</font><font style="display: inline;color:#1F497D;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">mandatory civil monetary penalties of between </font><font style="display: inline;">$11,181</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">$22,363</font><font style="display: inline;"> for each separate false claim, subject to annual adjustment for inflation.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Although the healthcare industry has seen numerous ongoing investigations related to compliance and billing practices, hospitals, in particular, continue to be a primary enforcement target for the Office of Inspector General (&#x201C;OIG&#x201D;), the Department of Justice (&#x201C;DOJ&#x201D;) and other governmental fraud and abuse programs. Certain of the Company&#x2019;s individual facilities have received, and from time to time, other facilities may receive, inquiries or subpoenas from </font><font style="display: inline;">Medicare Administrative Contractors, and </font><font style="display: inline;">federal and state agencies. Any </font><font style="display: inline;">proceedings against the Company may involve potentially substantial amounts as well as the possibility of civil, criminal, or administrative fines, penalties, or other sanctions, which could be material. Settlements of suits involving Medicare and Medicaid issues routinely require both monetary payments as well as corporate integrity agreements. </font><font style="display: inline;">Depending on whether the underlying conduct in these or future inquiries or investigations could be considered systemic, their resolution could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#x2019;s financial position, results of operations and liquidity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">In connection with the Company&#x2019;s acquisition of Marquette General, the seller self-disclosed various potentially non-compliant physician arrangements under the CMS</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">voluntary self-disclosure protocol. The Marquette General self-disclosures were settled with CMS as of April 14, 2017, for a total payment of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million.&nbsp; In accordance with the asset purchase agreement, the seller paid that amount in full to CMS.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the Company reversed the previously established reserve for settlement of the Marquette General self-disclosure and recognized a gain of </font><font style="display: inline;">$18.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$11.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million net of income taxes, or </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.28</font><font style="display: inline;"> per diluted share, which is included under the caption &#x201C;Other non-operating losses, net&#x201D; in the accompanying consolidated statements of income for the year ended December 31, 2017.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On September 16, 2013, the Company and </font><font style="display: inline;">two</font><font style="display: inline;"> of its affiliated hospitals, Vaughan Regional Medical Center, located in Selma, Alabama, and Raleigh General Hospital, located in Raleigh, West Virginia, made a voluntary self-disclosure to the Civil Division of the DOJ. The voluntary self-disclosure related to concerns regarding the clinical appropriateness of certain interventional cardiology procedures conducted by one physician in each of these hospitals&#x2019; cardiac catheterization laboratories. The Company cooperated with the government in its investigations of the voluntary self-disclosure and provided additional documentation, as requested. The Company believes that the government&#x2019;s investigations are now closed.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Following reviews by independent interventional cardiologists, the Company notified patients of these </font><font style="display: inline;">two</font><font style="display: inline;"> physicians who may have received an unnecessary procedure of such fact. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#x2003;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company and/or Vaughan Regional Medical Center and several of the Company&#x2019;s subsidiaries, as well as Dr. Seydi V. Aksut and certain parties unaffiliated with the Company, were named defendants in </font><font style="display: inline;">26</font><font style="display: inline;"> individual lawsuits filed since December 2014 in the Circuit Court of Dallas County, Alabama, alleging that patients at Vaughan Regional Medical Center underwent improper interventional cardiology procedures.&nbsp;&nbsp;These lawsuits, as they pertain to entities affiliated with the Company, were settled and dismissed in February 2017.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Two</font><font style="display: inline;"> putative class action lawsuits were filed in the Circuit Court of Dallas County, Alabama.&nbsp;&nbsp;The first putative class action lawsuit, filed in November 2014, sought certification of a class consisting of all Alabama citizens who underwent an invasive cardiology procedure at any Company-owned Alabama hospital and who received notice regarding the medical necessity of that procedure.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company reached an agreement in principle to settle this lawsuit, and on August 14, 2017, the Court entered an order certifying this class for settlement purposes only and granted the parties&#x2019; motion for preliminary approval of settlement.&nbsp;&nbsp;A fairness hearing to determine whether the settlement was fair, reasonable, and adequate, and whether it should be approved by the Court, </font><font style="display: inline;">was conducted on November 8, 2017, at which time the settlement was approved.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Court&#x2019;s Order Approving Settlement became final and non-appealable on January 2, 2018. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The second putative class action lawsuit, filed in February 2015 , sought certification of a class of individuals that underwent an interventional cardiology procedure that was not medically necessary and performed by Dr. Aksut, and asserted, among other claims, claims under the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act (&#x201C;RICO&#x201D;). </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="color:#0000FF;display: inline;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">In March 2015, the Company removed the second class action to the U.S. District Court in Mobile, Alabama which dismissed with prejudice the RICO claims and refused to exercise jurisdiction over the remaining state law claims, and the lawsuit was remanded for further proceedings.&nbsp;&nbsp;In July 2017, this lawsuit was settled and dismissed as it pertained to entities affiliated with the Company.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:14.4pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="color:#0000FF;display: inline;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">Additionally, the Company and </font><font style="color:#0000FF;display: inline;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">two</font><font style="color:#0000FF;display: inline;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"> of its subsidiaries, including Raleigh General Hospital, as well as Dr. Kenneth Glaser, have been named in </font><font style="color:#0000FF;display: inline;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">82</font><font style="color:#0000FF;display: inline;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"> individual lawsuits filed in the circuit court of Raleigh County, West Virginia.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Additionally</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">three</font><font style="display: inline;"> patients had notified Raleigh General Hospital of their claims and intent to file a lawsuit.&nbsp;&nbsp;These lawsuits and claims alleged that patients at Raleigh General Hospital underwent unnecessary interventional cardiology procedures.&nbsp;&nbsp;In January 2017, all parties to these lawsuits and claims entered into settlement agreements settling all claims against the Company, its subsidiaries, Raleigh General Hospital and Dr. Glaser.&nbsp;&nbsp;Following these settlements, </font><font style="display: inline;">two</font><font style="display: inline;"> additional lawsuits were filed against the same parties alleging the same claims.&nbsp;&nbsp;These two lawsuits were settled in March 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;In February 2017, the Company received a notice of claim with respect to a putative class action lawsuit in the Circuit Court of Raleigh County, West Virginia against it, </font><font style="display: inline;">two</font><font style="display: inline;"> of its subsidiaries, Raleigh General Hospital and Dr. Glaser, alleging that patients at Raleigh General Hospital underwent medically unnecessary interventional cardiology procedures and seeking to certify a class of such patients.&nbsp;&nbsp;The new claims seek compensatory and punitive damages, costs, attorneys&#x2019; fees and other available damages. </font>

During the year ended December 31, 2016, the Company recorded an accrual for loss contingencies for cardiology-related lawsuits, which resulted in a net expense of </font><font style="display: inline;">$24.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$15.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million net of income taxes, or </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.36</font><font style="display: inline;"> loss per diluted share.</font>

At December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">, these uncompleted projects had an esti</font><font style="display: inline;">mated cost to complete</font><font style="display: inline;"> of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$358.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million. 			<font style="display: inline;">In December 2015, the Company acquired a parcel of land in Marquette, Michigan, and in May 2016, began constructing a replacement hospital for the existing Marquette General.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company anticipates that it will continue to operate the existing hospital campus until such point that the replacement hospital is ready for its intended use.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management currently expects that the construction of the replacement hospital will conclude in early 2019.&nbsp; </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">In accordance with ASC 360-10, the Company performed an evaluation of the recoverability of the carrying values of certain of the assets of Marquette General which management anticipates disposing upon completion of the construction of the replacement hospital.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on this evaluation, the Company determined that the carrying value of the assets to be disposed were no longer recoverable from their estimated future cash flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the Company recognized an impairment loss of </font><font style="display: inline;">$34.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$21.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million net of income taxes, or </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.54</font><font style="display: inline;"> loss per diluted share, which is included under the caption &#x201C;Other non-operating losses, net&#x201D; in the consolidated statements of income for the year ended December 31, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;The impairment loss represents the write-down of the assets to their estimated fair value as measured under ASC 820-10, using estimated future net cash flows expected to be generated by market participants.&nbsp;&nbsp;The estimate of fair value is subject to change as the result of negotiations with interested parties, regulatory approvals, or changes in market conditions.</font>

Acquired companies may have unknown or contingent liabilities, including liabilities for failure to comply with healthcare laws and regulations, medical and general professional liabilities, workers compensation liabilities, previous tax liabilities and unacceptable business practices. Although the Company institutes policies designed to conform practices to its standards following completion of acquisitions, there can be no assurance that the Company will not become liable for past activities that may later be asserted to be improper by private plaintiffs or government agencies. Although the Company generally seeks to obtain indemnification from prospective sellers covering such matters, there can be no assurance that any such matter will be covered by indemnification, or if covered, that such indemnification will be adequate to cover potential losses and fines.</font>
